title: Contact Your Bank About Exposed Account and Routing Numbers
body_md:
Exposed account and routing numbers can be used to create counterfeit checks or initiate electronic withdrawals. Your bank or credit union can secure the account.

1. Call your bank or credit union and explain that the account and routing numbers may have been exposed in a reported data breach. Ask which protections it recommends; common options include closing the account and opening one with a new number, or adding extra verification to the existing account.
2. If you keep the account open, review activity regularly and turn on transaction alerts by text or email.
3. Report any withdrawal, transfer, or check you did not authorize as soon as you find it. Once notified, the institution generally has ten business days to investigate.
4. If you move to a new account number, update direct deposits and automatic payments promptly.

Guidance from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau on unauthorized transactions is at consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb (see "How do I get my money back after I discover an unauthorized transaction?"). Questions can also be directed to the CFPB at 855-411-2372.
